A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neurosymbolic Diffusion Models and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–H. Corresponding methods, experiments, and proofs can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original NESYDM experiments on MNIST Addition, visual path planning, and RSBench, plus majority-voting analyses in Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports loss-weight sensitivity experiments in Appendix H.2.

M1.justification: The model, three-part objective, variational posterior, gradient estimator, and sampling procedures are retained. The new output-prediction pseudocode combines the previously described sampler and majority voting; it does not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MNIST Addition, visual path-planning, MNIST-Half, MNIST-Even-Odd, and BDD-OIA coverage. The new loss-weight experiments reuse MNIST-Half and its existing ID/OOD scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments. Section G.4.1 explicitly identifies PNP as the baseline previously called DPL, explaining that its implementation did not actually use the DeepProbLog language.

E3.justification: New H.2 experiments evaluate conditional-entropy NESYDM on MNIST-Half, holding the output-loss weight at 1 while sweeping concept-loss and entropy weights. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, architectures, training settings, and prediction procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 analyses alternative majority-voting strategies; v2 retains that analysis and adds systematic sensitivity studies of two training-loss weights in H.2 and Tables 9–10. These substantially extend the analysis to training sensitivity and identify settings with strong label accuracy but poor concept accuracy and calibration.

E5.justification: H.2 specifies three repeated runs for the new ablations. The existing ten-seed main experimental protocol and Mann–Whitney testing at significance level 0.05 remain stated unchanged. Revised uncertainty values in Table 3 do not establish a changed estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 9–10 add substantive failure-mode results: some loss weights retain approximately 99% label accuracy while concept accuracy falls to approximately 42% and ID ECE reaches approximately 57%. Table 3 also revises existing scores, including conditional-entropy MNIST-Even-Odd OOD ECE from 11.17±1.35 to 5.77±0.98. Tables 1–2 and 7–8 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The NELBO theorems, assumptions, proofs, and gradient derivations are retained. Distinguishing concept and output vocabulary sizes with separate symbols clarifies notation; v1 already allowed unequal sizes. The new ECE discussion provides conceptual motivation rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: diffusion captures concept dependencies while enabling scalable neurosymbolic prediction and reasoning-shortcut awareness. Added analyses support or qualify these existing claims.

C2.justification: New Section G.4.2 explains the connection between concept calibration and reasoning-shortcut awareness, while acknowledging ECE as an imperfect proxy. H.2 interprets poor calibration under unsuitable loss weights as convergence onto a single reasoning shortcut and identifies the need for careful entropy-weight tuning.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies the baseline implementation and explicitly includes hyperparameter tuning in the estimated 600 GPU hours. However, Table 9 introduces a conflicting default-weight statement: its caption says 1e-06 was used, while Table 6 retains 1.5e-06. This does not establish an actual change to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Five references are added, covering DeepGraphLog, reasoning shortcuts, DeepSeekMath/GRPO, and discrete-diffusion surveying. Sections 2.2 and 5 refine the discussion of expressive probabilistic predictors and their scaling constraints, without replacing the paper's overall positioning.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact. Local revisions clarify terminology and related work, add the ECE-motivation subsection, and reorganize Appendix H into voting and loss-weight subsections. Some algorithm cross-references in F.1 become malformed.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–10, moves the training algorithm from the appendix into the main text, and adds a pseudocode display of the existing output-prediction procedure. Figures 1–2 and existing table structures are retained, with localized caption, header, and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The new H.2 ablations substantiate loss-weight sensitivity and expose calibration failures, while G.4.2 better explains and qualifies the measurement of reasoning-shortcut awareness. Main-text pseudocode and clearer baseline identification also help. These provide a modest net benefit despite unexplained Table 3 revisions and the new default-weight inconsistency between Tables 9 and 6.
